subject: Usage-to-Commit conversion path & invoice offset proposal
messages:
From: Akhil Rao <akhil@fastware.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@fastware.com
Date: 2027-05-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions — headroom usage & commit options

Laura,

Thanks for the call this morning. We ran a quick spike on our staging environment and consumed ~1.2M tokens in 36 hours — much higher than our monthly baseline. The immediate ask from engineering is a short-term buffer we can draw from automatically to avoid throttles during unpredictable bursts.

Two commercial questions from Procurement/Finance: 1) Can that buffer be provided as an on-demand "ephemeral allowance" that converts to a committed discount if used over 60% of the allowance in a quarter? 2) If conversion happens mid-month, do you provide a pro-rata credit against the next invoice for any overage we already paid at PAYG rates?

We're preparing for a June feature flag roll-out and need clarity on pricing/contract language so we can get PO issuance started.

— Akhil
CTO, FastWare Systems

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Akhil Rao <akhil@fastware.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial pricing questions — headroom usage & commit options

Akhil — thanks for the detail and the spike numbers. Short answer: yes, we can structure an on-demand buffer that has a conversion trigger and a pro-rata invoice path. I wanted to capture the proposal in writing so Procurement has something concrete.

Proposal (high level):
- Ephemeral Allowance: N tokens/month buffer (initially proposed 1.5M) billed PAYG while unused.
- Conversion Trigger: If consumption of the buffer >= 60% of allowance in any rolling 30-day window, the allowance converts into a committed monthly tier for the remainder of the contracted term.
- Pro-rata Offset: Any PAYG overage consumed in the current invoice period that converts will be credited back as an invoice offset equal to the difference between PAYG charges and the committed tier rate, pro-rated to the effective conversion date.
- Discounting: Committed tier discount applies from conversion date forward (we propose a 22% blended discount vs PAYG for the converted allowance at RW-4582 volume band).
- Fallbacks: If conversion is rejected within 7 business days (Procurement/Legal), Redwood will continue PAYG billing for that period and re-evaluate at next invoice.

I'll loop in Ben from Pricing to validate the math and Jordan for PO & billing flow. Attaching a redlineable proposal and the preliminary MCA for your legal team.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai; Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing math for RW-4582 (ephemeral allowance conversion)

Laura / Jordan — reviewed Akhil's numbers and Laura's proposal. Quick notes on calculations and constraints: 

1) Example math (assume buffer = 1.5M tokens):
   - PAYG rate: $0.0008 / token => if fully consumed = $1,200/month
   - Committed tier (proposed 22% off): effectively $0.000624 / token => $936/month
   - If conversion occurs on day 10 of a 30-day period after 600k tokens consumed at PAYG, the pro-rata credit = (PAYG_paid_for_consumed_tokens - committed_rate_for_consumed_tokens) pro-rated from conversion start date.

2) Minimum commitment term for converted allowance: 3 months (to avoid churn & administrative churn on small conversions). We can be flexible on term length in negotiation (3–6 months).

3) Invoice offset mechanics: We can apply as either (a) credit on next invoice, or (b) apply as one-time refund for the overage invoice (requires finance coordination). For fast execution, recommend credit on next invoice and a one-line note in the invoice PDF calling out the conversion delta.

4) Edge cases: rapid reciprocal conversions (convert/unconvert multiple times within a quarter) — propose a 30-day lock once converted to prevent flip-flopping.

I'll assemble a sample invoice line-item and update the attached PDF. Jordan, can you confirm PO acceptance workflow (Net-30 vs Net-45) and if Procurement needs a signed SOW for allowance?

— Ben
Principal Pricing Analyst, Redwood Inference

Akhil — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Summary and next steps so we can get PO signed by end of week: 

Summary of agreed commercial points (pending Procurement signature):
- Ephemeral Allowance: 1.5M tokens/month starting May 15 (initial trial month).
- Conversion Trigger: 60% consumption in rolling 30 days converts buffer to committed tier.
- Conversion Term: 3-month minimum on conversion; auto-renews unless canceled with 30-day notice.
- Discount: 22% blended off PAYG for converted allowance; applies from conversion date going forward.
- Invoice Offset: Credit applied to next invoice; Redwood will include a conversion credit line and supporting math.
- Lock Window: 30-day conversion lock to prevent repeated convert/unconvert cycles.

Operational asks from FastWare:
- Confirm PO terms (Net-30 or Net-45).
- Legal to return MCA redlines by COB Friday.

If Procurement is comfortable, Jordan will generate the SOW + PO acceptance language and I will route for signature. Akhil, I can fast-track activation on our side the day we receive signed PO.

Thanks —Laura
